title.zh: 卷一百〇八 表第九 外戚恩澤侯表
title.en: Volume 108 Tables 9: Families of the Imperial Consorts

sentences.zh: 古恩澤封有三，曰外戚，曰中官，曰嬖倖。

translations.literal: In antiquity there were three kinds of grace-bestowing enfeoffments, namely consort kin, palace eunuchs, and favored minions.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times enfeoffments granted as imperial favor fell into three kinds: maternal relatives of empresses, palace eunuchs, and favored courtiers.

sentences.zh: 明興，追崇外氏，廟貌之隆，爵超五等，而苗裔無攷，未及授官。

translations.literal: When the Ming arose, they posthumously honored the maternal clan; temple images rose in splendor and ranks surpassed the five grades, yet descendants had no examination credentials and had not yet received office.
translations.idiomatic: At the dynasty's founding the court exalted the empresses' maternal kin posthumously—temples rose in splendor and ranks exceeded the five enfeoffment grades—yet no descendant had passed the civil examinations or yet held official appointment.

sentences.zh: 高后外家不奉朝請，家法之嚴有自來矣。

translations.literal: The Empress Gao's maternal family did not attend court audiences; the severity of household law had long existed.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Gao's kin did not attend regular court audiences; the Ming house's strict restraint on affinal families dated back to the beginning.

sentences.zh: 自文皇后而外，率由儒族單門，入儷宸極。

translations.literal: Apart from Empress Wen, all were from single-branch Confucian clans who entered to match the imperial consort.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Wen, every consort came from a modest scholar-official family of no great connections before entering the palace.

sentences.zh: 后父初秩不過指揮，侯伯保傅以漸而進。

translations.literal: A queen's father's initial rank did not exceed commander; marquis, earl, guardian, and tutor advanced gradually.
translations.idiomatic: A consort's father at first received no rank higher than commander; titles of marquis, earl, guardian, and tutor came only step by step.

translations.literal: The favored received thick estates and fields, arrayed servants and slaves.
translations.idiomatic: The more favored were granted ample estates and staffed households of bondsmen and retainers.

sentences.zh: 雖擁侈富之資，曾無憑藉之勢，制防之微意寓焉。

translations.literal: Though possessing extravagant wealth, they never had leverage for power; the subtle intent of regulatory restraint lay therein.
translations.idiomatic: Though they might amass great wealth, they were never allowed political leverage—a restraint woven subtly into the system.

sentences.zh: 肅宗申明功令，裁抑世封，戚畹周親不得與汗馬餘勳為齒。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong clarified merit statutes, curtailed hereditary enfeoffments; consort kin and close relatives could not rank with the toils of battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongzhi Emperor re-affirmed the statutes of merit, cut back hereditary enfeoffment, and barred consort kin and close royal relatives from standing on equal footing with men who had earned honors in war.

translations.literal: Though called heart-and-liver, affairs ranked below enfeoffed lords.
translations.idiomatic: Though styled "imperial kin at heart," they were treated as inferior to meritorious enfeoffed lords in practice.

translations.literal: Viewing above to Han and Tang, they were nearly worlds apart.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with Han and Tang precedents, the gap was nearly absolute.

sentences.zh: 茲考實錄所載封襲歲月，備列為表，以別於元功之次。

translations.literal: Here we examine the years of enfeoffment and succession recorded in the Veritable Records, fully array as table, to distinguish from the order of founding merit.
translations.idiomatic: This table sets out the dates of initial enfeoffment and successive inheritance as recorded in the Veritable Records, distinguishing these grants from the roster of founders who won the dynasty by force.

sentences.zh: 他若宦官子弟濫列金貂，方士義兒均從班爵，騁文成之丕誕，踵養子之傾輈，亂政亟行，若循一軌，各依年次，備著於篇，亦班固表外戚，譜張釋、欒大之例也。

translations.literal: Other cases: eunuch sons recklessly arrayed in gold finery, Daoist masters' adoptive sons all following court ranks, Wen Cheng's wild boasts prospering, following adoptees' overturning, chaotic government urgently practiced as if one track, each according to year order fully set forth in the chapter, also like Ban Gu's table of consort kin, cataloguing Zhang Shizhi and Luan Da's examples.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs' sons who crowded the ranks in gold-trimmed caps, Daoist adepts' pseudo-sons who received court titles on equal terms, the grandiose claims of the magician Wen Cheng, the ruin that followed the elevation of adoptive heirs—in each case misrule ran on a single track. Listed below in chronological order, alongside entries for maternal kin, are those who resemble Zhang Shizhi and Luan Da in Ban Gu's table of imperial affines: favorites who corrupted government by grace rather than merit.

cells.content: 瑛庶兄。成化十六年三月庚寅襲。弘治六年十月卒。

translations.literal: Ying's elder brother by a concubine. Succeeded on gengyin in the third month of Chenghua 16. Died in the tenth month of Hongzhi 6.
translations.idiomatic: Elder half-brother of Ying by a concubine mother. He inherited the title on gengyin day in the third month of Chenghua 16 (1480) and died in the tenth month of Hongzhi 6 (1493).

cells.content: 弘治七年三月己亥襲。十二年鎮陝西，召還。十三年八月領左府。正德三年十二月提督團營，幷三千營管操。嘉靖十四年六月卒。贈太傅，諡康靖。

translations.literal: Succeeded on jihai in the third month of Hongzhi 7. In year 12 garrisoned Shaanxi, recalled. In the eighth month of year 13 directed Left Commission. In the twelfth month of Zhengde 3 supervised Training Corps, also Three Thousand camp commander. Died in the sixth month of Jiajing 14. Posthumously Grand Tutor, posthumous name Kangjing.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title on jihai day in the third month of Hongzhi 7 (1494). In Hongzhi 12 (1499) he was posted to garrison Shaanxi and then recalled; in the eighth month of Hongzhi 13 (1500) he headed the Left Military Commission. In the twelfth month of Zhengde 3 (1508) he supervised the Training Corps and also commanded the Three Thousand Camp. He died in the sixth month of Jiajing 14 (1535) and was posthumously made Grand Tutor with the posthumous name Kangjing.

translations.literal: Succeeded on bingwu in the fourth month of Jiajing 17, repeatedly directed camp affairs. Died on dingchou in the first month of year 29.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title on bingwu day in the fourth month of Jiajing 17 (1538) and repeatedly held camp commands. He died on dingchou day in the first month of Jiajing 29 (1550).

cells.content: 鑭從子。嘉靖三十四年二月辛巳襲。萬曆三十七年六月己未卒。

translations.literal: Lan's nephew. Succeeded on xinsi in the second month of Jiajing 34. Died on jiwei in the sixth month of Wanli 37.
translations.idiomatic: Nephew of Lan. He inherited the title on xinsi day in the second month of Jiajing 34 (1555) and died on jiwei day in the sixth month of Wanli 37 (1609).

cells.content: 萬曆三十七年十一月癸巳襲。崇禎元年七月己巳總京營。十月己亥革京營總督，聽議。十七年城陷，闔家自焚死。

translations.literal: Succeeded on guisi in the eleventh month of Wanli 37. In the seventh month of Chongzhen 1 on jisi overall director of Capital camps. In the tenth month on jihai abolished Capital camps director, awaiting deliberation. In year 17 when city fell, whole family self-immolated and died.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title on guisi day in the eleventh month of Wanli 37 (1609). On jisi day in the seventh month of Chongzhen 1 (1628) he took overall command of the Capital camps; on jihai day in the tenth month the post of Capital camps director was abolished and he awaited court deliberation. When the city fell in Chongzhen 17 (1644) the whole family burned themselves to death.

cells.content: 景帝母吳太后兄。景泰中封。天順元年二月除。

translations.literal: Elder brother of Emperor Jingdi's mother Empress Dowager Wu. Enfeoffed in Jingtai reign. Abolished in the second month of Tianshun 1.
translations.idiomatic: Elder brother of the Jingdi Emperor's mother, Empress Dowager Wu. Enfeoffed during the Jingtai reign; the title was abolished in the second month of Tianshun 1 (1457).

cells.content: 內臣曹吉祥嗣子。天順元年十二月以吉祥奪門功封。五年七月謀反，伏誅。

translations.literal: Adopted son of eunuch Cao Jixiang. In the twelfth month of Tianshun 1 enfeoffed for Jixiang's Gate-Seizing merit. In the seventh month of year 5 plotted rebellion, executed.

cells.content: 憲宗母孝肅太后父。成化四年四月甲午追封。十七年十二月加贈寧國公，諡榮靖。

translations.literal: Father of Emperor Xiaozong's mother Empress Dowager Xiaosu. Posthumously enfeoffed on jiawu in the fourth month of Chenghua 4. In the twelfth month of year 17 further posthumously Duke of Ning, posthumous name Rongjing.
translations.idiomatic: Father of the Xiaozong Emperor's mother, Empress Dowager Xiaosu. Posthumously enfeoffed on jiawu day in the fourth month of Chenghua 4 (1468). In the twelfth month of Chenghua 17 (1481) he was further posthumously made Duke of Ning with the posthumous name Rongjing.

cells.content: 成化三年十一月乙亥封慶雲伯。四年予世襲。十七年十二月進封侯。弘治元年加祿百石。正德四年二月卒。贈宣國公，諡恭和。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of Chenghua 3 on yihai enfeoffed Earl of Qingyun. In year 4 granted hereditary. In the twelfth month of year 17 advanced to marquis. In Hongzhi 1 added stipend of one hundred shi. Died in the second month of Zhengde 4. Posthumously Duke of Xuan, posthumous name Gonghe.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai day in the eleventh month of Chenghua 3 (1467) he was made Earl of Qingyun; in Chenghua 4 (1468) the title was made hereditary; in the twelfth month of Chenghua 17 (1481) he was advanced to marquis; in Hongzhi 1 (1488) his stipend was increased by one hundred shi. He died in the second month of Zhengde 4 (1509) and was posthumously made Duke of Xuan with the posthumous name Gonghe.

translations.literal: Grandson of Empress Rui's younger brother Zhong. Enfeoffed on gengchen in the first month of Chenghua 15. In the fourth month of Hongzhi 2 granted hereditary. Died in the intercalary twelfth month of Jiajing 4.
translations.idiomatic: Grandson of Empress Rui's younger brother Zhong. Enfeoffed on gengchen day in the first month of Chenghua 15 (1479). In the fourth month of Hongzhi 2 (1489) the title was made hereditary. He died in the intercalary twelfth month of Jiajing 4 (1525).

translations.literal: Succeeded on yimao in the eighth month of Jiajing 5. Later abolished by statute.

cells.content: 純皇后弟。成化二十年十一月封伯，世襲。弘治元年加祿百石。六年追封源父鎮阜國公，進源爵侯。嘉靖三年七月丁卯卒。贈太師，諡榮靖。

translations.literal: Younger brother of Empress Chun. In the eleventh month of Chenghua 20 enfeoffed as earl, hereditary. In Hongzhi 1 added stipend of one hundred shi. In year 6 posthumously enfeoffed Yuan's father as Duke of Zhenfu, advanced Yuan to marquis. Died on dingmao in the seventh month of Jiajing 3. Posthumously Grand Preceptor, posthumous name Rongjing.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother of Empress Chun. Enfeoffed as earl in the eleventh month of Chenghua 20 (1484); the title was hereditary. In Hongzhi 1 (1488) his stipend was increased by one hundred shi. In Hongzhi 6 (1493) Yuan's father was posthumously made Duke of Zhenfu and Yuan was advanced to marquis. He died on dingmao day in the seventh month of Jiajing 3 (1524) and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor with the posthumous name Rongjing.

translations.idiomatic: He inherited the earldom on dingchou day in the eleventh month of Jiajing 3 (1524); the line was later abolished under the revised rules.

cells.content: 能子，壽弟。成化二十一年封，世襲。弘治元年加祿百石。正德三年十二月卒。

translations.literal: Son of Neng, younger brother of Shou. Enfeoffed in Chenghua 21, hereditary. In Hongzhi 1 added stipend of one hundred shi. Died in the twelfth month of Zhengde 3.
translations.idiomatic: Son of Zhou Neng and younger brother of Zhou Shou. Enfeoffed in Chenghua 21 (1485); the title was hereditary. In Hongzhi 1 (1488) his stipend was increased by one hundred shi. He died in the twelfth month of Zhengde 3 (1508).

translations.literal: Succeeded in the second month of Zhengde 4. Died in the third month of year 14.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title in the second month of Zhengde 4 (1509) and died in the third month of Zhengde 14 (1519).

cells.content: 正德十四年七月襲。嘉靖三十八年六月甲子卒。以例除。

translations.literal: Succeeded in the seventh month of Zhengde 14. Died on jiazi in the sixth month of Jiajing 38. Abolished by statute.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title in the seventh month of Zhengde 14 (1519) and died on jiazi day in the sixth month of Jiajing 38 (1559). The line was abolished under the revised rules.

translations.literal: Father of Empress Jing. On jiwei in the second month of Hongzhi 4 enfeoffed as earl; in the third month of year 5 advanced to marquis; died in the eighth month. Posthumously Duke of Chang, posthumous name Zhuangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Father of Empress Jing. Enfeoffed as earl on jiwei day in the second month of Hongzhi 4 (1491), advanced to marquis in the third month of Hongzhi 5 (1492), and died in the eighth month. He was posthumously made Duke of Chang with the posthumous name Zhuangsu.

translations.literal: Son of Luan, younger brother of Heling. On yichou in the fourth month of Hongzhi 8 enfeoffed as earl. In the ninth month of year 16 advanced to marquis. In the third month of Jiajing 1 added Grand Tutor. On bingzi in the tenth month of year 12 imprisoned and sentenced to death, rank abolished.

Enfeoffed as earl on yichou day in the fourth month of Hongzhi 8 (1495), advanced to marquis in the ninth month of Hongzhi 16 (1503), and made Grand Tutor in the third month of Jiajing 1 (1522). On bingzi day in the tenth month of Jiajing 12 (1533) he was imprisoned, sentenced to death, and stripped of his title.

cells.content: 萬曆三十七年襲伯。四十五年二月辛亥進侯。天啟七年八月戊戌加太子太師。崇禎十一年正月卒。

translations.literal: Succeeded as earl in Wanli 37. In the second month of year 45 on xinhai advanced to marquis. In the eighth month of Tianqi 7 on wuxu added Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent. Died in the first month of Chongzhen 11.

He died in the first month of Chongzhen 11 (1638).

translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title on xinwei day in the first month of Wanli 35 (1607).

translations.literal: Father of the Guangzong Emperor's mother Empress Dowager Xiaojing. Enfeoffed when Guangzong ascended. Died in Chongzhen 14.
translations.idiomatic: Father of the Guangzong Emperor's mother, Empress Dowager Xiaojing. Enfeoffed when the Guangzong Emperor acceded. He died in Chongzhen 14 (1641).

cells.content: 熹宗母孝和太后弟。天啟元年閏二月封伯，尋進侯。崇禎八年卒。

translations.literal: Younger brother of the Xizong Emperor's mother Empress Dowager Xiaohe. In the intercalary second month of Tianqi 1 enfeoffed as earl, soon advanced to marquis. Died in Chongzhen 8.

translations.literal: Succeeded on wuyin in the twelfth month of Chongzhen 9. Died at the hands of bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title on wuyin day in the twelfth month of Chongzhen 9 (1636) and was killed by the rebels.

translations.literal: Father of the Xizong Emperor's empress. In Tianqi 1 enfeoffed as earl. In the eleventh month of Chongzhen 11 advanced to marquis. Died at the hands of bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Father of the Xizong Emperor's empress. Enfeoffed as earl in Tianqi 1 (1621), advanced to marquis in the eleventh month of Chongzhen 11 (1638). He was killed by the rebels.

cells.content: 內臣魏忠賢姪。天啟六年三月封肅寧伯，進侯。十月戊申進封公。七年八月丙申加太師。莊烈帝即位，伏誅。

translations.literal: Nephew of eunuch Wei Zhongxian. In the third month of Tianqi 6 enfeoffed as Earl of Suning, advanced to marquis. In the tenth month on wushen advanced to duke. In the eighth month of year 7 on bingshen added Grand Preceptor. When the Zhuanglie Emperor ascended, executed.
translations.idiomatic: Nephew of the eunuch Wei Zhongxian. In the third month of Tianqi 6 (1626) he was made Earl of Suning and advanced to marquis; in the tenth month on wushen day he was raised to duke; in the eighth month of Tianqi 7 (1627) on bingshen day he was made Grand Preceptor. When the Chongzhen Emperor acceded he was executed.

translations.literal: Zhongxian's grandnephew. Enfeoffed on jimao in the seventh month of Tianqi 7. In the eighth month on bingshen added Junior Preceptor. When the Zhuanglie Emperor ascended, executed.

translations.literal: Younger brother of Liangqing. Enfeoffed on yisi in the eighth month of Tianqi 7. When the Zhuanglie Emperor ascended, executed.

cells.content: 莊烈帝母孝純太后弟。莊烈帝即位封。崇禎八年卒。九年，贈侯，予三代誥。十三年九月，父應元追封瀛國公。

translations.literal: Younger brother of the Zhuanglie Emperor's mother Empress Dowager Xiaochun. Enfeoffed when Zhuanglie ascended. Died in Chongzhen 8. In year 9 posthumously marquis, granted edicts for three generations. In the ninth month of year 13, father Yingyuan posthumously Duke of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother of the Chongzhen Emperor's mother, Empress Dowager Xiaochun. Enfeoffed when the Chongzhen Emperor acceded. He died in Chongzhen 8 (1635); in Chongzhen 9 (1636) he was posthumously raised to marquis and edicts were granted for three generations of ancestors; in the ninth month of Chongzhen 13 (1640) his father Liu Yingyuan was posthumously made Duke of Ying.

translations.literal: Succeeded on jiazi in the twelfth month of Chongzhen 9. In the ninth month of year 13 added Junior Tutor. In the third month of year 17 died in calamity.

translations.idiomatic: Father of the Chongzhen Emperor's empress. Enfeoffed in Chongzhen 3 (1630). In Chongzhen 17 (1644), when the capital fell, he was taken prisoner.
